1	Quick spec — Pi model logo
2	- Add a Pi extension that includes the selected model in its terminal title, preserving the session/project name.
3	- Refresh the title on session start, restoration and model_select; reuse Radar’s existing model-to-logo mapping.
4	- Deploy on Darkseid and Alghul, without changing Hermes or hardcoding a provider.
5	- Unknown models show no model logo, never a guessed one.
6	- Acceptance: tests cover startup, restoration, model switching and unknown models; live checks confirm the correct logo beside Pi’s logo on both hosts.
7	- Rollback: remove the extension and restore Pi’s normal title; no upgrades or paid model requests required.

Quick spec — Pi model logo
- Add a Pi extension that includes the selected model in its terminal title, preserving the session/project name.
- Refresh the title on session start, restoration and model_select; reuse Radar’s existing model-to-logo mapping.
- Deploy on Darkseid and Alghul, without changing Hermes or hardcoding a provider.
- Unknown models show no model logo, never a guessed one.
- Acceptance: tests cover startup, restoration, model switching and unknown models; live checks confirm the correct logo beside Pi’s logo on both hosts.
- Rollback: remove the extension and restore Pi’s normal title; no upgrades or paid model requests required.

3	// Which mark stands for which agent.
4	//
5	// The font variant uses Private Use Area codepoints from the bundled
6	// HerdrAgentIconsMax face; the text variant uses ordinary Unicode that renders
7	// in any terminal font. `auto` picks the font when the terminal can actually
8	// reach it, which on Linux means asking Fontconfig — macOS and Windows have no
9	// equivalent query, so there `auto` stays conservative and uses text. Set
10	// `variant = "font"` explicitly once the font is installed.
11	
12	const { spawnSync } = require('node:child_process');
13	const config = require('./config');
14	
15	const FONT_FAMILY = 'Herdr Agent Icons Max';
16	
17	const PUA = {
18	  claude: '',
19	  codex: '',
20	  opencode: '',
21	  omp: '',
22	  cline: '',

36	  agy: '',
37	  kiro: '',
38	  amp: '',
39	  devin: '',
40	  qodercli: '',
41	  glm: '',
42	};

44	// The lifecycle marks live in our own font for the same reason the logos do:
45	// `✓ ○ ◌` are missing from plenty of monospace faces, and a terminal that falls
46	// back to a CJK face draws them at full width — a circle sized for a Han
47	// character sitting next to text that is not. Borrowed Unicode looked fine on
48	// Windows and oversized on macOS purely by luck of the fallback chain.
49	// The three idle tiers deliberately share ONE mark. They used to differ in
50	// shape as well as colour \u2014 filled disc, ring, dot \u2014 because shape survives
51	// where colour fails. That was written when the sidebar had no ordering and
52	// the tier was the only way to find a live session among thirty. Sorting by
53	// activity does that job now, so three shapes for one concept became noise:
54	// a column of identical marks with a colour gradient reads faster than three
55	// glyphs the eye must first learn. E1C4/E1C5 stay in the font, unused, so
56	// this is three lines to revert.
57	//
58	// The mark is the RING and not the dot because it shares its row with Herdr's
59	// cell separator, which is itself a middot \u2014 a dot that means "state" and a
60	// dot that means "next field" are the same handful of pixels. The ring is
61	// scaled down in font/codepoints.toml so it still reads as a marker beside
62	// the title rather than a bullet in front of it.
63	// `working` takes the same ring as the idle tiers rather than a spinner of
64	// its own: the motion is the braille frames in front of the title, and two
65	// things animating inside one entry fight each other. Its ring is painted in
66	// the brand colour, so the row still says "this one is busy" at a glance.
67	const STATE_PUA = {
68	  working: '',
69	  done: '\ue1c0',
70	  blocked: '\ue1c1',
71	  idle: '\ue1c2',
72	  unknown: '\ue1c3',
73	  idle_fresh: '\ue1c2',
74	  idle_stale: '\ue1c2',
75	};
76	
77	// How many spinner steps one half of the blocked pulse lasts. Five is about
78	// three quarters of a second a side: slow enough to read as a heartbeat rather
79	// than a flicker, quick enough that a row waiting on an answer is noticed
80	// before the eye has finished the line.
81	const PULSE_STEPS = 5;
82	
83	// The mark in front of a blocked row, pulsing.
84	//
85	// A question mark that never moves is a question mark you stop seeing. Blocked
86	// is the one state that costs something to ignore — the agent is stopped until
87	// a person answers — and it was the only event mark with no motion at all,
88	// sitting in a column beside the marks of rows that need nothing.
89	//
90	// Codex says the same thing in its terminal title, alternating `[ ! ]` with
91	// `[ . ]` while it waits, and that is the shape borrowed here: the loud mark
92	// and a quiet one take turns in one cell. Both halves are one cell wide, so
93	// nothing beside it shifts, and the colour never changes — the pulse reads as
94	// one mark breathing, not as two marks swapping.
95	function blockedFrame(step, variant = config.variant) {
96	  const quiet = Math.floor(step / PULSE_STEPS) % 2 === 1;
97	  return stateGlyph(quiet ? 'idle' : 'blocked', variant);
98	}
99	
100	const TEXT = {
101	  claude: '§',
102	  codex: 'Λ',
103	  opencode: '◇',
104	  omp: 'Π',
105	  cline: '∇',
106	  mastracode: '∑',
107	  kimi: '✨',

118	  grok: '✖',
119	  agy: '△',

121	  amp: 'Ʌ',
122	  devin: 'ꓓ',
123	  qodercli: 'Ǫ',
124	  glm: 'Ƶ',
125	};

127	// What an agent is called, for the rows whose own terminal title never says.
128	//
129	// Most agents write their name into the title and the row simply shows it —
130	// `Claude Code`, `grok`. The ones below leave the title to the shell, which
131	// fills it with the working directory, so the row reads `notes` under a group
132	// header that already says `notes`, or `~/src/notes: agy - agy`. The name
133	// goes in instead (see lib/state.js), which is the one thing those rows were
134	// missing and the logo beside them cannot spell.
135	//
136	// Keyed by the id Herdr reports, which is why Antigravity is `agy` here and
137	// in every other table, and why this table is where that abbreviation is
138	// turned back into something readable.
139	const DISPLAY = {
140	  claude: 'Claude Code',
141	  codex: 'Codex',
142	  opencode: 'OpenCode',
143	  omp: 'Oh My Pi',
144	  cline: 'Cline',
145	  mastracode: 'Mastra',
146	  kimi: 'Kimi',
147	  kilo: 'Kilo',

153	  deepseek: 'DeepSeek',
154	  gemini: 'Gemini',
155	  gpt: 'GPT',
156	  qwen: 'Qwen',
157	  grok: 'grok',
158	  agy: 'Antigravity',
159	  kiro: 'Kiro',
160	  amp: 'Amp',
161	  devin: 'Devin',
162	  qodercli: 'Qoder',
163	  glm: 'GLM',
164	};
165	
166	let fontChecked = false;
167	let fontPresent = false;
168	
169	function fontAvailable() {
170	  if (fontChecked) return fontPresent;
171	  fontChecked = true;
172	  // The copy this plugin installed itself (bin/install-font.js) counts on
173	  // every platform; fontconfig below is the only other oracle, Linux-only.
174	  try {
175	    if (require('./font').isInstalled()) return (fontPresent = true);
176	  } catch {
177	    // Fall through to fontconfig.
178	  }
179	  try {
180	    const result = spawnSync('fc-match', ['--format', '%{family}\n', FONT_FAMILY], {
181	      encoding: 'utf8',
182	      timeout: 3000,
183	      windowsHide: true,
184	    });
185	    fontPresent =
186	      result.status === 0 &&
187	      String(result.stdout)
188	        .split(/[\n,]/)
189	        .some((name) => name.trim() === FONT_FAMILY);
190	  } catch {
191	    fontPresent = false;
192	  }
193	  return fontPresent;
194	}

196	// Which of the two glyph tables is in play. `auto` asks whether the icon font
197	// is actually installed; every other value is taken at its word.
198	function resolveVariant(variant = config.variant) {
199	  if (variant === 'none') return 'none';
200	  return variant === 'auto' ? (fontAvailable() ? 'font' : 'text') : variant;
201	}
202	
203	// vendor -> the exact string this machine will publish for it. The sidebar
204	// block matches on these values (managed-config colours `$logo` by rule), so
205	// the block and the daemon have to read the table through the same door.
206	function glyphs(variant = config.variant) {
207	  const resolved = resolveVariant(variant);
208	  if (resolved === 'none') return {};
209	  return { ...(resolved === 'font' ? PUA : TEXT) };
210	}
211	
212	// The mark for `agent`, or null when this agent has none. Agents Herdr detects
213	// but this plugin has no mark for are left unmarked rather than given a
214	// stand-in that would read as the wrong vendor.
215	function logoFor(agent, variant = config.variant) {
216	  if (!agent || !(agent in PUA) || variant === 'none') return null;
217	  const resolved = resolveVariant(variant);
218	  return resolved === 'font' ? PUA[agent] : TEXT[agent];
219	}
220	
221	// What to call `agent`, or null when this plugin has no name for it — the
222	// same rule the marks follow: an agent we do not recognise is left as Herdr
223	// reported it rather than given a stand-in.
224	function nameFor(agent) {
225	  return DISPLAY[agent] ?? null;
226	}
227	
228	// The mark for a lifecycle state. An explicit config choice always wins;
229	// otherwise the variant decides, exactly as it does for logos. `none` is not
230	// honoured here — a state line with no state mark is not a state line.
231	function stateGlyph(state, variant = config.variant) {
232	  const chosen = config.userGlyph(state);
233	  if (chosen) return chosen;
234	  const resolved = resolveVariant(variant);
235	  // A state the face has no mark for falls back to its text mark rather than
236	  // to nothing: a missing glyph swallows the whole state line, and a pane with
237	  // no state line renders as a bare title at the margin — which reads as a
238	  // group header. That is how idle_fresh painted a second workspace title.
239	  if (resolved === 'font' && STATE_PUA[state]) return STATE_PUA[state];
240	  return config.STATIC_GLYPH[state];
241	}
242	
243	// local patch (2026-09-27): which model family a pane runs, for the model mark
244	// beside the harness logo. Read off the title (Hermes and our statuslines put
245	// the model id there); harnesses tied to one family fall back to it.
246	// Keys are PUA names above. Add a family: one regex line + a glyph in PUA.
247	const MODEL_FAMILIES = [
248	  ['claude', /\b(claude|opus|sonnet|haiku|fable)\b/i],
249	  ['gpt', /\b(gpt|o[1-9](-\w+)?|codex)\b/i],
250	  ['gemini', /\bgemini\b/i],
251	  ['deepseek', /\bdeepseek\b/i],
252	  ['qwen', /\bqwen\b/i],
253	  ['grok', /\bgrok\b/i],
254	  ['glm', /\bglm\b/i],
255	  ['kimi', /\b(kimi|moonshot)\b/i],
256	];
257	const MODEL_FALLBACK = { claude: 'claude', codex: 'gpt', gemini: 'gemini' };
258	
259	function modelFor(title, agent) {
260	  for (const [family, re] of MODEL_FAMILIES) if (re.test(title ?? '')) return family;
261	  return MODEL_FALLBACK[agent] ?? null;
262	}
263	
264	module.exports = {
265	  modelFor,
266	  logoFor,
267	  nameFor,
268	  blockedFrame,
269	  PULSE_STEPS,
270	  glyphs,
271	  resolveVariant,
272	  stateGlyph,
273	  STATE_PUA,
274	  PUA,
275	  TEXT,
276	  DISPLAY,
277	  FONT_FAMILY,
278	  fontAvailable,
279	};

### Across machines

Pick one machine as the hub. List the others as `peers`, by SSH host name:

```json
{ "groups": ["NOW", "REVIEW"], "panes": {}, "peers": ["buildbox"] }
```

The hub keeps one SSH link per peer and syncs every move. Each peer needs:

- The plugin at the same path under `$HOME` as on the hub.
- `ssh <peer>` working without a prompt.
- `node` on the `PATH` of a non-interactive SSH shell.

herdr plugin action invoke 4242labs.herdr-radar-plus.unconfigure

24	  table once. A copy in your own config used to refuse the whole install —
25	  and was only noticed in its header form: `custom.name = …` under `[theme]`,
26	  or an inline table, slipped past, the block was appended on top, and Herdr
27	  fell back to defaults for the entire file, taking every plugin with it.

30	  Herdr's, with your own theme table your colours stay. The note says which

32	  config it misjudges ever turns up, the effect is a skipped block and a
33	  note, never a broken file.

38	  is now posted as a Herdr notification as well.

# Changelog

## 0.42.0 — 2026-09-27

First release of herdr-radar-plus, built on herdr-radar 1.3.15. Plugin id
`4242labs.herdr-radar-plus`, so it installs beside nothing: remove herdr-radar first.

- **Attention view.** Blocked and done agents first, idle next,
  working last, newest first inside each tier. `view-flip` steps through active, attention
  and recent.
- **Named groups.** `lane-up` and `lane-down` move the focused agent between the groups named
  in `lanes.json`. A divider names each group once two have members.
- **Groups across machines.** A hub lists its `peers`, and `bin/lane-sync.js` keeps groups in
  step over SSH. `presence.json` makes sure each group gets one divider across all machines.
- **Model mark.** A model-family logo beside the harness logo, read from the pane title.
- **Machine row.** A second line under each agent names its machine.

Everything below is herdr-radar's history, kept as it was.

## 1.3.15 — 2026-09-25

- **A table you already have keeps only its block out.** The plugin writes
  `[theme.custom]` and the `[ui.sidebar.*]` tables itself, and TOML allows a
  table once. A copy in your own config used to refuse the whole install —
  and was only noticed in its header form: `custom.name = …` under `[theme]`,
  or an inline table, slipped past, the block was appended on top, and Herdr
  fell back to defaults for the entire file, taking every plugin with it.
  Every form is seen now, and the block that would collide stays out while
  the others install: with your own sidebar tables the Agents panel stays
  Herdr's, with your own theme table your colours stay. The note says which
  block and why. The check reads the file as TOML, not as lines; if a
  config it misjudges ever turns up, the effect is a skipped block and a
  note, never a broken file.

- **The reason reaches the screen.** Herdr shows a failed action as
  `failed (exit 1)` and files the output in the plugin log, which nobody
  installing for the first time knows to read. A skipped block or a refusal
  is now posted as a Herdr notification as well.

- **A write is checked before it is kept.** Every change to `config.toml` is
  followed by `herdr config check`; on a parse error the file is restored
  from the backup and the parser's message becomes the note. A warning, such
  as an unknown key, is not a parse error and does not block.
